info.title: Glassmkr Dashboard API
info.description:
Programmatic access to Glassmkr Dashboard for fleet management. Authentication is via Bearer token: gmk_acct_live_* for account API keys, gmk_cru_live_* for collector keys (telemetry only).

See https://glassmkr.com/docs for the full reference. This document covers the v1 stable surface.

This document is the machine contract for the routes it lists. It does not yet cover every route the product serves; scripts/check-openapi-drift.mjs enforces that everything listed here exists, and tracks what is still undocumented so the gap cannot grow silently.

Errors: every response under /api/ with a status of 400 or above returns the ApiError schema below. Branch on `error`, never on `message`.

Contract notes an agent should not have to infer. Cursor pagination exists on GET /servers and GET /account/audit only; other list endpoints return a complete result. Idempotency-Key is honoured on POST /servers only. GET /servers/{id}/health carries an explicit freshness block; other reads do not yet, so judge their age from the data itself.

servers.description: Self-hosted: set origin to your dashboard's base URL

origin.description: Scheme and host of your dashboard

AccountApiKey.description: Account-level API key for management endpoints. Created at /api/v1/account/keys (requires recent re-authentication via /api/v1/account/verify-password).

CollectorKey.description: Server-scoped collector key for /api/v1/ingest only. Cannot read or write any other resource.

SessionCookie.name: guardian_token
SessionCookie.description: Browser session cookie, issued by the sign-in flow at /api/v1/auth/login. An API client cannot obtain one: there is no programmatic exchange from an account key to a session. An operation that lists ONLY this scheme is therefore not callable with any API key, by design. Creating, rotating and revoking account keys are the operations in that category, because in v1 an account key may not mint or replace another account key.

ApiError.description: Returned by every /api/ response with status >= 400.

error.description: Stable machine code. Branch on this.

message.description: Human explanation. Wording may change at any time; do not parse.

retryable.description: Whether an identical retry could plausibly succeed.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Stripe-style idempotency token. If a request retries within 24h, the cached response is returned.

GET /servers.description: Returns all servers owned by the authenticated customer. Paginated by `cursor`. Cursor-paginated: pass `cursor` from a previous response's `next_cursor`. An absent `next_cursor` means the last page.

POST /servers.description: Registers a new server, returns the collector key (gmk_cru_live_*) once. The plaintext key cannot be retrieved later; rotate via /api/v1/servers/{id}/rotate-key to issue a new one. Accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header. A retry within 24 hours carrying the same key returns the original response rather than creating a second server. This is the only mutation that supports it today; assume the others are not safe to retry blindly.

hostname.description: RFC 1035 hostname; opaque label, never resolved server-side. Defaults to name.

api_key.description: Plaintext collector key. Save it now; not shown again.

GET /servers/{id}.description: Management-plane detail for one server: identity, OS, hardware, agent version, last seen. Telemetry lives on /servers/{id}/health and /servers/{id}/metrics.

PATCH /servers/{id}.description: Update name and/or tags. Hostname is intentionally NOT updatable — operations relies on it as a stable identifier.

DELETE /servers/{id}.summary: Delete a server (moves it to trash)
DELETE /servers/{id}.description: Moves the server to trash. It stops collecting and drops out of your node count, and it is restorable with POST /servers/{id}/restore. Requires ?confirm=true. This is the same behaviour as the MCP tool glassmkr.admin.delete_server; every interface agrees. To destroy a server permanently, delete it here first and then call DELETE /trashed-servers/{id}, which is a separate operation with its own capability. Side effects: the server stops collecting and drops out of the billed node count. Both reverse on restore.

POST /servers/{id}/rotate-key.description: Atomically revokes the current collector key for this server and returns a new gmk_cru_live_* key. Old key returns 401 immediately. Per-endpoint rate limit: 10/hour/account.

collector_key.description: New plaintext key, gmk_cru_live_*. Not shown again.

200.description: Key metadata. Key material is never returned.

GET /account/keys.description: Metadata for this account's keys: name, prefix, last four, scope, capabilities, expiry, last use. Key material is never returned; it is shown once at creation and never again.

POST /account/keys.description: Requires recent re-authentication (POST /api/v1/account/verify-password within last 5 min). Returns plaintext once; not shown again.

expires_at.description: Optional future timestamp. Key auto-revokes after.

scope.description: Hierarchical access level, fixed at creation. read < write < admin. A `scopes` array was accepted in early v1 and its column was dropped by migration 020; sending it now has no effect.

capabilities.description: Opt-in capabilities, additive to `scope` and never implied by it. Empty by default. servers:purge permits DELETE /trashed-servers/{id}. Requires write or admin scope.

201.description: Created. `key` is shown once and never again.

key.description: The full credential. Store it now; it cannot be retrieved later.

DELETE /account/keys/{id}.description: Revokes a key immediately. A rotated key's predecessor carries a grace period instead; this does not.

POST /account/keys/{id}/rotate.description: Atomically revokes the old key and mints a new one with the same name + scopes + expires_at. Requires recent re-authentication. Per-endpoint rate limit: 10/hour/account. Side effect: the previous credential keeps working for a grace period rather than dying immediately, so a rotation does not break a running agent mid-collection.

200.description: Rotated. The previous credential keeps working for a grace period.

POST /account/verify-password.description: Used to gate sensitive operations like API key creation. Auth: session only.

GET /account/audit.description: Customer-facing view of api_audit_log. Filterable. Entries are append-only: the schema blocks UPDATE and DELETE (migrations/postgres/009), and no retention job removes them. Cursor-paginated, newest first, via `next_cursor`.

POST /ingest.description: Telemetry-only endpoint. Auth: collector key (gmk_cru_live_* or legacy col_*). Rate limit: 1 request per minute per server.

storage.description: Disks, SMART attributes, filesystems, RAID and ZFS state.

ipmi.description: BMC sensors and SEL, when a BMC is present.

DELETE /trashed-servers/{id}.description: PERMANENT and irreversible: destroys the server row and its stored metrics. Four conditions, all required. (1) The server must ALREADY be in the trash, so DELETE /servers/{id} is an unavoidable first step. (2) ?confirm=true. (3) Recent re-authentication via POST /account/verify-password, so a leaked key alone is not enough. (4) An account key holding the servers:purge capability, which is opt-in at key creation and is NOT granted by admin scope, so keys created before it existed cannot purge. Deliberately absent from the MCP surface: an agent has no path to permanent destruction.

GET /health.description: Liveness and dependency checks. Public: no credential needed, so an uptime monitor can call it.

GET /version.description: The Crucible version this deployment considers current, and the minimum it supports. Read by the agent's own update check.

GET /host-profiles.description: The host-profile catalogue. A profile suppresses alerts that are expected by design for a kind of host; real faults still fire. Static product metadata, identical for every account.

GET /servers/{id}/health.description: The most recent health rollup for one server: current alert state and the domain summaries behind it. This is the endpoint to poll for current state; /servers/{id}/alerts is the alert list itself. The response carries a `freshness` block: `observed_at`, `age_seconds`, `stale`, and the `stale_after_seconds` threshold it used, so a caller can apply its own. `stale` is true beyond fifteen minutes, which is three missed collections at the five-minute cadence. Treat a stale reading as evidence the host stopped reporting, not as current state.

GET /servers/{id}/alerts.description: Alerts for one server. Use ?status=active for what is currently firing; the default returns the fuller set, which includes history.

GET /servers/{id}/history.description: Historical snapshots for one server, bounded. Exceeding the maximum window returns 400 with the limit and what was requested, so a client can retry with a smaller range rather than guessing.

GET /servers/{id}/metrics.description: Metric series for one server over a bounded window.

200.description: Metric series over a bounded window.

GET /servers/{id}/disk-health.description: SMART-derived health per drive, including the reallocated and pending counters that drive the storage rules.

GET /servers/{id}/trend-warnings.description: Active trend warnings for one server. Urgency tiers and what they mean are documented at https://glassmkr.com/docs.

GET /servers/{id}/analyses.description: Previously generated AI analyses for one server. Reading costs nothing; generating a new one is POST /servers/{id}/analyze.

POST /servers/{id}/analyze.description: Generates a new AI analysis of this server's recent snapshots. Self-hosted instances point LLM_API_URL at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; with none configured the feature is off and everything else still works.

POST /servers/{id}/restore.description: Returns a soft-deleted server to active. Subject to the account's node cap, so a restore can be refused when the fleet is already at the limit. Side effect: re-activating a server counts against the account's node cap, so a restore can be refused when the fleet is already at the limit.

POST /servers/restore-all.description: Bulk form of the above, same node-cap rules.

POST /alerts/{id}/acknowledge.description: Marks an alert acknowledged. It stays visible and does not stop the underlying condition; acknowledgement records that a human has seen it.

POST /alerts/{id}/resolve.description: Marks an alert resolved. Alerts normally auto-resolve when the condition clears; use this when the state cannot clear itself.

note.description: Optional reason recorded in the audit log.

GET /channels.description: Configured alert destinations. Six types: slack, discord, pagerduty, telegram, email, webhook.

config.description: Type-specific destination. slack and discord take webhook_url; telegram a chat_id; email an address; pagerduty a routing_key; webhook a url.

priorities.description: Which alert priorities route here. Omitted means all.

DELETE /channels/{id}.description: Removes a channel. Alerts stop routing to it.

POST /channels/{id}/test.description: ALWAYS returns 200. A delivery failure is a result, not an API error: the test ran and found out the channel did not accept the message. Read `success`; when false, `error` carries the upstream reason. Side effect: this actually delivers a message to the configured destination. It is a real notification, not a simulation.

GET /trend-warnings/evaluations.description: When the trend engine last ran and what it covered. Batches run every six hours.

200.description: Batch history. Batches run every six hours.

GET /trend-warnings/track-record.description: Confirmed and dismissed counts, and a precision estimate. Below ten ratings the estimate is a tally rather than a measurement, and the dashboard says so.

200.description: Counts and a precision estimate. Below ten ratings the estimate is a tally, not a measurement.

POST /trend-warnings/{id}/feedback.description: Records a warning as valuable or a false positive. Feeds the precision estimate above.

GET /servers/{id}/alerts/{alertId}/ticke.description: Builds a plain-text ticket from an alert using a deterministic template. Glassmkr does not contact your provider: the draft is yours to review, edit and send.

PUT /channels/{id}.description: Full replacement. PATCH updates individual fields.

POST /servers/{id}/mutes.summary: Mute a rule on a server
POST /servers/{id}/mutes.description: Stops one rule firing for this server. A mute can resolve an alert that is currently active for that rule, so the effect is not confined to the future. Side effect: muting a rule can resolve an alert that is currently active for it, so this is not confined to future evaluations.

200.description: Muted. May also resolve an alert currently active for that rule.

alert_type.description: Rule id to mute on this server.

DELETE /servers/{id}/mutes.description: The rule can fire again on the next evaluation.

POST /servers/{id}/alerts/{alertId}/tick.description: Builds a plain-text ticket from an alert using a deterministic template: no model call and no third-party network. POST by REST convention only; it changes no customer state.

200.description: Draft ticket text. Nothing is sent anywhere.

GET /servers/{id}/analyze.description: Status of an analysis started with POST on the same path.

DELETE /trend-warnings/{id}/feedback.description: Removes a previously recorded rating, which also removes it from the precision estimate.

GET /billing/status.description: Plan, node usage against the cap, and retention window. Self-hosted instances have no plan gates, so this reports the deployment's configuration rather than a tier.
